CHN.note: China is the world's largest fish producer (~67 Mt incl. aquaculture, FAO FishStat) and #1 net seafood importer. For frozen fish HS 0303, WITS 2024 shows imports of 2,376 kt — Russia alone supplied 1,012 kt of frozen pollock/cod. Much is re-processed and re-exported.

JPN.note: Japan is a top-3 seafood importer. WITS 2024: 549 kt of frozen fish HS 0303 (gross), led by Chile (104 kt salmon/trout), USA (96 kt), Norway (65 kt), Russia (51 kt). Total seafood imports (all HS) far exceed the 0303 line.

USA.note: Major seafood importer (~$25bn all-product). WITS 2024 frozen fish HS 0303: ~212 kt gross (value $1.07bn), led by China (66 kt re-exported whitefish), Brazil (16 kt), Norway (17 kt). Shrimp (0306) and fillets (0304) dominate US seafood imports beyond this line.

KOR.note: South Korea is a large frozen-fish importer. WITS 2024 HS 0303: 535 kt gross, led by Russia (219 kt pollock), China (101 kt), Norway (37 kt mackerel). Russia supplies ~41% — notable single-supplier concentration.

ESP.note: Spain has the EU's highest seafood consumption and a large distant-water fleet. WITS 2024 HS 0303: 274 kt gross, led by Morocco (37 kt), Portugal (33 kt), Seychelles (23 kt tuna), Namibia (hake). Many flows are tuna/hake from West-African and Indian-Ocean waters.

EGY.note: Egypt is Africa's largest aquaculture producer (~2 Mt tilapia) but still imports frozen fish for cheap animal protein. WITS 2024 HS 0303: 199 kt gross, led by Oman (45 kt), Norway (44 kt mackerel), Netherlands (34 kt). Frozen mackerel/herring is a food-security staple for low-income households.

NGA.note: Nigeria is one of the world's biggest frozen-fish importers and a critical food-security case: cheap frozen mackerel/horse-mackerel ('Titus', 'kote') is a primary animal protein. WITS 2023 (latest reported) HS 0303: ~327 kt gross ($607M), led by Chile (83 kt), Ireland (40 kt), Netherlands (32 kt), Korea (29 kt), Russia (23 kt). 2024 not yet reported by Nigeria.

CIV.note: Cote d'Ivoire is a major West-African frozen-fish importer; frozen mackerel/sardinella is a dietary staple. CIV does not report HS 0303 imports to UN Comtrade for 2024 (non-reporter); this balance is a FAO/GLOBEFISH-based estimate, not a WITS figure.

GHA.note: Ghana imports large volumes of frozen mackerel/horse-mackerel as small-pelagic stocks decline. Ghana is a weak/non-reporter for HS 0303 in Comtrade 2024; this is a FAO/GLOBEFISH estimate rather than WITS-sourced.

NOR.note: Norway is the world's #1 farmed-salmon producer and #2 seafood exporter by value (~NOK 175bn, 2024). For frozen fish HS 0303 it ships mackerel, herring and salmon worldwide — a top-5 supplier to China (138 kt), Japan (65 kt), Egypt (44 kt), Korea (37 kt).

CHL.note: Chile is the #2 salmon producer and a major exporter of frozen salmon, trout, jack mackerel and hake. WITS importer data shows Chile as #1 supplier to Japan (104 kt) and a leading supplier to Nigeria (83 kt, 2023).

RUS.note: Russia is a top wild-capture nation (Bering Sea/Sea of Okhotsk pollock, cod) and the single largest supplier of frozen fish to Asia. WITS 2024: Russia shipped 1,012 kt to China and 219 kt to Korea (HS 0303). Sanctions redirected much whitefish from the EU/US toward China.

VNM.note: Vietnam is a top-5 seafood exporter (pangasius, tuna, shrimp) and also imports raw frozen fish for processing/re-export. WITS 2024 shows Vietnam supplying 94 kt to China (HS 0303); much of Vietnam's export value is fillets (0304) and shrimp (0306).

IND.note: India is the world's #2 fish producer (mostly inland aquaculture) and a top shrimp exporter. For frozen fish HS 0303 it supplies 153 kt to China (low-value marine fish/ribbonfish). India's flagship seafood export is frozen shrimp (0306), outside this line.

ECU.note: Ecuador is the world's largest farmed-shrimp exporter; its frozen-fish (HS 0303) trade is smaller — tuna and small pelagics. WITS 2024 shows Ecuador supplying 12 kt to Spain and 10 kt to China. Its dominant line is frozen shrimp (0306).

ISL.note: Iceland is a wild-capture powerhouse (cod, capelin, mackerel, redfish) exporting nearly all output. WITS 2024 shows Iceland supplying 31 kt to China and 9 kt to Japan (HS 0303). Seafood is Iceland's leading goods export.

rankings.note: Importers are 2024 WITS/UN Comtrade gross-import quantities for frozen fish HS 0303 (Nigeria = 2023, latest reported; totals summed from partner rows). Exporter ranking is an FAO/GLOBEFISH-based ordering of frozen-fish + total-seafood export tonnage and is approximate. These are HS 0303 (frozen whole fish) only: shrimp (0306), fillets (0304) and fresh (0302) are large separate trades, especially for India, Ecuador, Vietnam, Norway.

companies.name: Mowi ASA
companies.metric: World's largest Atlantic-salmon farmer; ~500 kt harvested, revenue ~EUR 5.5bn (FY2024).
companies.note: Vertically integrated salmon producer (Norway, Scotland, Chile, Canada) supplying fresh and frozen salmon globally; a bellwether showing up in Norway's and Chile's HS 0303 flows.
companies.improve: Should publish frozen-vs-fresh split and destination-country volumes, plus feed (fishmeal/soy) sourcing by origin.

companies.name: Thai Union Group
companies.metric: World's largest canned-tuna company; revenue ~US$3.9bn (FY2024); Chicken of the Sea, John West, Petit Navire.
companies.note: Global tuna and seafood processor sourcing frozen raw tuna (much under HS 0303) from the Pacific and Indian Oceans; a re-export hub.
companies.improve: Should disclose frozen-tuna raw-material volumes by flag/ocean and IUU-risk screening rates.

companies.name: Maruha Nichiro
companies.metric: Japan's largest seafood company; revenue ~US$6.5bn (FY2024); global catching, farming, trading, processing.
companies.note: Major buyer/trader of frozen fish (pollock, salmon, mackerel) feeding Japan's import-dependent market — a key counterparty in the Chile/USA/Russia→Japan flows.
companies.improve: Should report frozen-fish procurement by source country and species to quantify Japan's import dependence.

companies.name: Nissui (Nippon Suisan)
companies.metric: Major Japanese seafood multinational; revenue ~US$5bn (FY2024); operations in Japan, the Americas, Europe.
companies.note: Global whitefish (Alaska pollock, hake) and salmon supplier with North American and European subsidiaries; a significant mover of frozen fish into Japan, the US and the EU.
companies.improve: Should publish origin-level frozen-fish volumes and the share of Russian-origin pollock (directly or via Chinese reprocessing).

companies.name: Cooke Inc.
companies.metric: Privately held global seafood group; salmon farming plus wild-capture (Wanchese, Omega Protein); revenue >US$3bn.
companies.note: Diversified producer/trader of farmed salmon and wild-caught fish across the Americas and Europe, contributing to Canada/US/Chile HS 0303 flows.
companies.improve: Private; should publish frozen-fish output and destination splits, plus fishmeal/reduction-fishery volumes (Omega Protein).

companies.name: Leroy Seafood Group
companies.metric: Second-largest Norwegian salmon/trout producer; revenue ~US$3bn (FY2024); farming, wild-catch (whitefish), processing.
companies.note: Major Norwegian exporter of frozen and fresh salmon, trout and whitefish; a contributor to Norway's HS 0303 flows to Asia, the EU and Africa.
companies.improve: Should break out frozen-product export tonnage by destination region and report whitefish (cod/saithe) frozen volumes separately from salmon.

global.note: Production = total world fisheries + aquaculture output (~190 Mt live weight in 2024, aquaculture now >50%), FAO FishStat/SOFIA basis; consumption = food fish supply (non-food/reduction uses excluded). Exports here = world frozen-fish HS 0303 trade only (~14-15 Mt; total seafood trade across all HS lines is far larger at ~60+ Mt / ~US$190bn). FAO-based estimates, rounded; 2024 provisional.

forecast.method: OECD-FAO Agricultural Outlook / FAO SOFIA envelope; 2030=2024×(1+rate)^6. Production growth driven almost entirely by aquaculture (capture fisheries near flat); frozen-fish trade grows with output and cold-chain expansion in Asia and Africa.
